name: OpenJarvis setup guide
description: OpenJarvis, the free open-source assistant from the reel: eight assistants that run on your own computer, including a morning digest that reads your day out loud from your email and calendar.

page.title: Set up your own Jarvis
page.sub: OpenJarvis is the free, open-source assistant from the reel, built at Stanford. Eight assistants run on your own computer: research with sources, code, an all-day monitor, and a spoken morning digest from your email and calendar.
page.prompt_how: Paste this into Claude Code (the Code tab in the Claude desktop app, not the normal chat).
page.prompt_note: The install is one command and takes about three minutes on a good connection. Claude asks before it runs it.
page.tested_title: We checked it against its own page

results.name: Built at Stanford, runs on your own computer

page.tested_text: We read the project's own page: **17,277 stars**, Apache 2.0 licence, built at Stanford's Hazy Research and Scaling Intelligence Lab. It ships **eight assistants**: the morning digest, deep research with citations, a monitor that runs all day, a code assistant and four more. The installer sets everything up with one command in **about three minutes**, and one sign-in connects Gmail, Calendar and Tasks for the digest. **Not checked by us:** installing and running it on our own computer.
page.tip: **The tip:** start with the morning digest only. Connect your email and calendar, hear one briefing, then add the next assistant when you want it.

prompt:
https://github.com/open-jarvis/OpenJarvis

Install this for me, then set up the morning digest. Tell me each step before you run it.

followups.label: Hear your first briefing
followups.prompt: Connect my Gmail and Calendar, then generate and play my first morning digest.
followups.note: One sign-in covers Gmail, Calendar and Tasks. The digest is read out loud.

followups.label: Research something
followups.prompt: Use the deep research assistant on this question and show me the sources: [your question]
followups.note: It searches the web and your own documents and cites what it used.

followups.label: Watch something for me
followups.prompt: Set up the monitor to check [what you want watched] every hour and tell me when it changes.
followups.note: The monitor keeps running in the background with its own memory.

checklist_title: Set it up in five steps

checklist.title: Open Claude Code
checklist.detail: The Code tab in the Claude desktop app (or the claude command in a terminal), on a paid Claude plan. You can also install OpenJarvis without Claude: its page has a one-line installer for Mac, Windows and Linux.

checklist.title: Paste the link and the request
checklist.detail: Claude reads the project's install steps and runs the one-command installer. It takes about three minutes on a good connection.

checklist.title: Give it about three minutes
checklist.detail: It downloads and sets itself up on your own computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.

checklist.title: Connect email and calendar
checklist.detail: One Google sign-in covers Gmail, Calendar and Tasks. This is what the morning digest reads.

checklist.title: Play your first digest
checklist.detail: Ask for your first morning digest. After that it can run every morning on its own.

safety: **It runs on your own computer.** That is the point of it, and it means it is only as fast as your machine. An older laptop will feel slow.
**You choose what it connects to.** Only connect the email and calendar you want it to read.
**It is a research project.** Expect rough edges and updates; check the project's page if something fails.
**We have not installed it ourselves yet.** Everything here is from the project's own page.
